answers.text: Three lines, same order, every time — drop-off time, pallet count, damage noted.
It should list time, customer, topic and outcome.
The finish time doesn't add up — six hours from an 8am start shouldn't run into the next day.
96 to 118 is more than a 20% rise. The on-time rate might be worth checking too.
Output 2, clearly — the numbers behind the 88% are shown. Output 1 doesn't show them.
Email 2 — real volume figures. Email 1 doesn't say what it's comparing to.
1. No. 2. Yes. 3. Yes, should be fine. 4. No. 5. No.
The hourly rates should be redacted, and the non-disclosure clause needs care too.
I'd cross-check the stock counts against the system before the summary goes out.
Step 1 carries risk downstream, but step 4 — automatic submission — is where the gate really matters.
